page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-60 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance supplies 60 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 30 physical cores with two threads per core, supported by 240.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. Cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES cryptography, BMI2, ADX, and FMA operations. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs, relying exclusively on remote persistent disk options for block storage.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced compute capacity across single-core and multi-threaded applications, recording a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 61,473.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,210.0. Memory throughput performs strongly on uncached large-block transfers, reaching 226.55 GB/sec for read operations and 97.28 GB/sec for write workloads. The processor's vector extension profile is reflected in a PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 54,838.03, ranking in the upper 25th percentile. Similarly, PassMark database operations achieved a strong mark of 22,356.86. Conversely, token generation benchmarks on quantized small and medium language models showed weaker throughput, registering 60.5 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 8.75 tokens/sec on a 7B model due to the lack of dedicated tensor acceleration.

The c2-standard-60 provides high compute density and strong memory throughput for CPU-bound tasks without requiring specialized hardware accelerators. Without local NVMe drives, storage performance depends on network-attached storage provisioned separately. The instance is suitable for continuous integration and compilation workflows, data analytics transformations, high-throughput web serving, and relational database hosting where high clock speeds and vector execution units are prioritized.

In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates strong uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 226.55 GB/sec and upper-quartile PassMark database and extended instruction test scores. Due to its balanced memory allocation, vector execution capabilities, and high core count, the c2-standard-60 is suited for software build pipelines, scientific simulations, relational database workloads, and compute-heavy batch processing.
